title: Amsterdam Declaration on Funding Research Software Sustainability (Draft v0.3, March 2023)
executive_summary: The Amsterdam Declaration on Funding Research Software Sustainability (March 2023, draft v0.3) highlights the critical role of research software and its developers in enabling reliable, reproducible, and impactful research across disciplines. It calls for global, coordinated action by funders to ensure the long-term sustainability of research software through improved funding policies, recognition, and support for the people and infrastructure involved. The Declaration outlines 12 key recommendations for funders, including promoting open-source practices, incentivizing reuse, integrating software into open science policies, supporting training and career progression, and considering ethical, environmental, and social impacts. The aim is to foster a healthy research software ecosystem by aligning funding instruments with both sustainability and innovation, and by encouraging collaboration across institutional and national boundaries. The Declaration is a first step toward formalizing global principles and best practices for funding research software sustainability.
characteristics: Emphasises the critical role of research software and its developers in ensuring reliable, accessible, and reproducible research outcomes across all disciplines.
Advocates for the sustainability of research software through integration into the research process, long-term funding, and recognition of the people involved.
Recommends funders stimulate documentation, licensing, open-source distribution, reuse, and improvement of research software, and include it in open science policies.
Calls for coordinated, global efforts among funders (public, private, philanthropic) to support research software ecosystems, including infrastructure, communities, and personnel.
Stresses the importance of training, hiring, and rewarding research software professionals, and recognising software as a research output in its own right.
Encourages ethical considerations, including responsible indicators for software impact, environmental and social impacts, and diversity, equity, and inclusion in research software sustainability.

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should stimulate the documentation, licensing, open-source distribution and accessibility of research software to enable the reproducibility of research outcomes.
kpi_list.target_description: Stimulate documentation, licensing, open-source distribution, and accessibility of research software to enable reproducibility
kpi_list.measurement_method: Assessment of policies and funding requirements supporting documentation, licensing, open-source distribution, and accessibility

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should incentivize the reuse and improvement of existing research software.
kpi_list.target_description: Incentivize reuse and improvement of existing research software
kpi_list.measurement_method: Review of funding calls and project outcomes for evidence of reuse and improvement

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should include research software in open science policies, following the principle ‘as open as possible, as closed as necessary’.
kpi_list.metric_name: Inclusion of Research Software in Open Science Policies
kpi_list.target_description: Include research software in open science policies according to openness principle

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should stimulate the development and maintenance of a research software ecosystem, including people, communities, and infrastructure, to ensure research software sustainability.
kpi_list.metric_name: Research Software Ecosystem Development and Maintenance
kpi_list.target_description: Stimulate development and maintenance of a research software ecosystem (people, communities, infrastructure)
kpi_list.measurement_method: Evaluation of funded projects and ecosystem support initiatives

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders (including public, private, and philanthropic) should be aware of each others' investments and work in a coordinated manner, as the research software ecosystem exceeds institutional and national boundaries.
kpi_list.target_description: Coordinate investments and activities across funders to support the research software ecosystem
kpi_list.measurement_method: Evidence of joint initiatives, shared reporting, or collaborative funding mechanisms

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should ensure that funding instruments are fit for purpose for both sustainability and innovation, so that research software is both maintained and developed for the longer term, to encourage a healthy research software ecosystem.
kpi_list.metric_name: Fit-for-Purpose Funding Instruments for Research Software
kpi_list.target_description: Ensure funding instruments support both sustainability and innovation in research software
kpi_list.measurement_method: Review of funding instrument design and outcomes

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should stimulate the training, hiring, and funding of both professional research and technical staff able to reuse, develop, and maintain sustainable research software.
kpi_list.metric_name: Research Software Personnel Training and Support
kpi_list.target_description: Stimulate training, hiring, and funding of staff for sustainable research software
kpi_list.measurement_method: Tracking of funded training programs, hiring initiatives, and personnel support

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should consider the value and impact of research software as a research output in its own right, to facilitate appropriate reward and recognition measures that enable career progression for all people involved.
kpi_list.metric_name: Recognition of Research Software as Research Output
kpi_list.target_description: Facilitate reward and recognition of research software as a research output for career progression
kpi_list.measurement_method: Inclusion of research software in evaluation and reward systems

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should require responsible citation practices for research software that recognise all contributors.
kpi_list.target_description: Require responsible citation practices for research software recognizing all contributors
kpi_list.measurement_method: Review of citation policies and compliance in funded projects

kpi_list.kpi_text: Funders should encourage the responsible use of appropriate indicators to assess the degree of permanence, reusability, and impact of research software.
kpi_list.metric_name: Assessment of Research Software Permanence, Reusability, and Impact
kpi_list.target_description: Encourage use of indicators to assess permanence, reusability, and impact of research software
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring of indicator adoption and reporting in funded projects

sdg_alignment: SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions

top_actors.name: Research Funding Organisations
top_actors.justification: Research funding organisations are the primary focus of the Declaration, which is addressed to them and calls for their action. They are repeatedly mentioned as the key actors responsible for enabling, sustaining, and coordinating research software sustainability through funding policies, instruments, and practices. Their influence is central to all recommendations and the main topics discussed.

top_actors.name: Research Software Alliance
top_actors.justification: The Research Software Alliance (ReSA) is highlighted as a key initiator and organiser of the Declaration and related workshops. It plays a leading role in developing awareness, convening stakeholders, and shaping the global agenda for research software sustainability. Its participation in key initiatives and decisions is explicitly mentioned.

top_actors.name: Researchers
top_actors.justification: Researchers, including those who develop and maintain research software, are repeatedly referenced as essential to the research software ecosystem. Their work is central to the sustainability and quality of research software, and they are the main beneficiaries of the recommended changes. Their recognition, training, and career progression are key topics in the document.

top_themes.name: Digital Sustainability
top_themes.justification: The entire document is centered on the sustainability of research software, emphasizing the need for long-term maintenance, funding, and support. The concept of sustainability is repeatedly discussed as the core objective, with recommendations and commitments directly addressing how to achieve it. It is the main message and strategic focus of the declaration.

top_themes.name: Digital Ecosystem
top_themes.justification: The document frames research software sustainability within the context of a 'research software ecosystem,' highlighting the interdependence of software, people, institutions, and funders. Much content is dedicated to ecosystem-level thinking, including recommendations for coordinated action, infrastructure, and community support, making this theme central to the document's approach and commitments.

top_themes.name: Digital Policy
top_themes.justification: A significant portion of the document is devoted to the role of funders and the need for policy changes to support research software sustainability. The declaration itself is a policy instrument, and the recommendations focus on funding practices, open science policies, and recognition of software as a research output, making digital policy a key lever for achieving the document's objectives.
